description:
Narrow response members to what Resend returns. The spec leaves almost every response member optional and few nullable, so callers had to check fields that are always there. A member is required where resend-node, the maintained official SDK, declares it non-optional and every live response (2026-10-29) carried it, and nullable where resend-node allows null or a live response held null: for example `bcc`, `cc` and `reply_to` are null when unset, `message_id` is null while an email is scheduled, and resend-node types `html`, `text` and `topic_id` as nullable. Domain claims and OAuth grants follow resend-node alone, without a live check: a claim needs the domain held by a second team, a paid feature, and a grant needs an authorized OAuth app. A broadcast recipient's `count` and `clicked_links` stay optional: they appear only for the opened and clicked types.

Every DNS record a domain returns carries `record`, `name`, `type`, `ttl`, `status` and `value`; the spec marks all of them optional. Live createDomain and getDomain responses (2026-10-29: 30 records across fresh, sending, receiving and tracking domains, in DKIM, SPF, Receiving and Tracking records of types TXT, CNAME and MX, both `not_started` and `verified`) always had all six, `ttl` as a string. They are now required on DomainRecord, which createDomain and getDomain share. `priority` stays optional: only MX records carry it.
